arxiv-2103-14774.title: A Generalized Multivariable Newton Method
arxiv-2103-14774.creator: Regina S. Burachik, Bethany I. Caldwell, C. Yalçın Kaya
arxiv-2103-14774.description: Abstract It is well known that the Newton method may not converge when the initial guess does not belong to a specific quadratic convergence region. We propose a family of new variants of the Newton method with the potential advantage of having a larger convergence region as well as more desirable properties near a solution.

arxiv-2106-15084.title: Exact Logit-Based Product Design
arxiv-2106-15084.creator: İrem Akchen, Velibor V. Mišić
arxiv-2106-15084.description: Abstract The share-of-choice product design (SOCPD) problem is to find the product, as defined by its attributes, that maximizes market share arising from a collection of customer types or segments. When customers follow a logit model of choice, the market share is given by a weighted sum of logistic probabilities, leading to the logit-based share-of-choice product design problem.

arxiv-2109-14592.creator: Justin Otter, Adam Ginsburg, Nicholas P. Ballering, John Bally, J.A. Eisner, Ciriaco Goddi, Richard Plambeck, Melvyn Wright
arxiv-2109-14592.description: Abstract The Orion Nebula Cluster (ONC) is the nearest dense star-forming region at ∼ \sim 400 pc away, making it an ideal target to study the impact of high stellar density and proximity to massive stars (the Trapezium) on protoplanetary disk evolution.

arxiv-2204-06614.title: Accurate Clinical Toxicity Prediction using Multi-task Deep Neural Nets and Contrastive Molecular Explanations
arxiv-2204-06614.creator: Bhanushee Sharma, Vijil Chenthamarakshan, Amit Dhurandhar, Shiranee Pereira, James A. Hendler, Jonathan S. Dordick, Payel Das
arxiv-2204-06614.description: Abstract Explainable machine learning for molecular toxicity prediction is a promising approach for efficient drug development and chemical safety. A predictive ML model of toxicity can reduce experimental cost and time while mitigating ethical concerns by significantly reducing animal and clinical testing.

arxiv-2208-08555.title: Wave functions and edge states in rectangular honeycomb lattices revisited: nanoflakes, armchair and zigzag nanoribbons and nanotubes
arxiv-2208-08555.creator: Anton Talkachov, Egor Babaev
arxiv-2208-08555.description: Abstract Properties of bulk and boundaries of materials can, in general, be quite different, both for topological and non-topological reasons. One of the simplest boundary problems to pose is the tight-binding problem of noninteracting electrons on a finite honeycomb lattice. Despite its simplicity, the problem is quite rich and directly related to the physics of graphene.

arxiv-2212-07191.title: Kinetics and steady state of polar flock with birth and death
arxiv-2212-07191.creator: Pratikshya Jena 1, Shradha Mishra 1
arxiv-2212-07191.description: Abstract We study a collection of polar self-propelled particles or polar flock on a two dimensional substrate with birth and death. Most of the previous studies of polar flock with birth and death have assumed the compressible flock, such that the local density of flock is completely ignored.

arxiv-2306-08408.title: Autothermotaxis of volatile drops
arxiv-2306-08408.creator: Pallav Kant, Mathieu Souzy, Nayoung Kim, Devaraj van der Meer, Detlef Lohse
arxiv-2306-08408.description: Abstract When a drop of a volatile liquid is deposited on a uniformly heated wettable, thermally conducting substrate, one expects to see it spread into a thin film and evaporate. Contrary to this intuition, due to thermal Marangoni contraction the deposited drop contracts into a spherical-cap-shaped puddle, with a finite apparent contact angle.

arxiv-2409-06378.title: Note on the existence of classical solutions of derivative semilinear models for one dimensional wave equation
arxiv-2409-06378.creator: Yuki Haruyama, Takiko Sasaki, and Hiroyuki Takamura
arxiv-2409-06378.description: Abstract This note is a supplement with a new result to the review paper by Takamura [ 13 ] on nonlinear wave equations in one space dimension. We are focusing here to the long-time existence of classical solutions of semilinear wave equations in one space dimension, especially with derivative nonlinear terms of product-type.

arxiv-2503-00234.title: Investigating the Relationship Between Debiasing and Artifact Removal using Saliency Maps
arxiv-2503-00234.creator: Lukasz Sztukiewicz, Ignacy Stępka, Michał WilińskiJerzy StefanowskiInstitute of Computing Science, Poznan University of Technology
arxiv-2503-00234.description: Abstract The widespread adoption of machine learning systems has raised critical concerns about fairness and bias, making mitigating harmful biases essential for AI development. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between debiasing and removing artifacts in neural networks for computer vision tasks.

arxiv-2506-02619.title: HGOT: Self-supervised Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with Optimal Transport
arxiv-2506-02619.creator: Yanbei Liu, Chongxu Wang, Zhitao Xiao, Lei Geng, Yanwei Pang, Xiao Wang
arxiv-2506-02619.description: Abstract Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks (HGNNs), have demonstrated excellent capabilities in processing heterogeneous information networks. Self-supervised learning on heterogeneous graphs, especially contrastive self-supervised strategy, shows great potential when there are no labels. However, this approach requires the use of carefully designed graph augmentation strategies and the selection of positive and negative samples.

arxiv-2509-15285.title: Simultaneous Speedmeter and Position-Meter Response in a Single Tabletop Interferometer
arxiv-2509-15285.creator: Roman Schnabel
arxiv-2509-15285.description: Abstract Quantum radiation-pressure noise (QRPN) limits the low-frequency sensitivity of gravitational wave detectors. The established method for suppressing QRPN is the injection of frequency-dependent squeezed light. It requires long-baseline filter cavities introducing substantial experimental complexity. A completely different interferometer concept is the speedmeter. It avoids QRPN at the source by measuring test mass speed instead of position.

arxiv-2510-00454.title: Measuring and Controlling the Spectral Bias for Self-Supervised Image Denoising
arxiv-2510-00454.creator: 1 st Wang Zhang, Huaqiu Li ∗, 2 nd Xiaowan Hu, 3 nd Tao Jiang, 4 nd Zikang Chen, Haoqian Wang†
arxiv-2510-00454.description: Abstract Current self-supervised denoising methods for paired noisy images typically involve mapping one noisy image through the network to the other noisy image. However, after measuring the spectral bias of such methods using our proposed Image Pair Frequency-Band Similarity, it suffers from two practical limitations. Firstly, the high-frequency structural details in images are not preserved well enough.

arxiv-2601-00785.title: FedHypeVAE: Federated Learning with Hypernetwork-Generated Conditional VAEs for Differentially-Private Embedding Sharing
arxiv-2601-00785.creator: Sunny Gupta, Amit Sethi
arxiv-2601-00785.description: Abstract Federated data sharing promises utility without centralizing raw data, yet existing embedding-level generators struggle under non-IID client heterogeneity and provide limited formal protection against gradient leakage. We propose FedHypeVAE , a differentially private, hypernetwork-driven framework for synthesizing embedding-level data across decentralized clients.

arxiv-2601-20181.title: A Fokker-Planck Framework for Control of Epidemics
arxiv-2601-20181.creator: Christian Parkinson and Souvik Roy
arxiv-2601-20181.description: Abstract . We present a control framework for stochastic compartmental models in epidemiology. In this framework, rather than directly controlling the stochastic system, we perform optimal control of an associated Fokker-Planck equation, with the goal of steering the distribution of possible solutions of the stochastic system to some desirable state.

pmc-10600234.title: Peptide binder design with inverse folding and protein structure prediction
pmc-10600234.creator: Patrick Bryant, Arne Elofsson
pmc-10600234.description: The computational design of peptide binders towards a specific protein interface can aid diagnostic and therapeutic efforts. Here, we design peptide binders by combining the known structural space searched with Foldseek, the protein design method ESM-IF1, and AlphaFold2 (AF) in a joint framework. Foldseek generates backbone seeds for a modified version of ESM-IF1 adapted to protein complexes.

pmc-11442495.title: Comparison of different types of single-port laparoscopic surgery in posterior uterine fibroid resection
pmc-11442495.creator: Qiannan Hou, Xin Li, Lu Huang, Qiang Zhang, Dan Feng, Yan Li, Dingqian Gu, Yonghong Lin, Li He
pmc-11442495.description: This study aims to objectively assess the effect of three surgical approaches for posterior uterine fibroid resection: transumbilical laparoendoscopic single-site surgery (LESS), vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) in prone position (vNOTES-P), and vNOTES in the lithotomy position (vNOTES-L).

pmc-12589623.title: Probabilistic dermal risk assessment for shallow groundwater users in agricultural settings of Saudi Arabia
pmc-12589623.creator: Husnain Haider, Md Shafiquzzaman, Mohammad T Alresheedi, Abdul Razzaq Ghumman, Abdullah Alodah, Muhammad Junaid
pmc-12589623.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Elevated salinity in unconfined aquifers limits residents’ use of groundwater for drinking in agricultural settings in KSA. The study developed a probabilistic dermal risk assessment methodology for heavy metals exposure through washing and bathing activities in farms across the Qassim Region, which addressed the uncertainties associated with limited data and vagueness in site-specific exposure factors, such as skin surface area and body weight.

pmc-12638914.title: Synergistic anticancer effects of Chrysin and trastuzumab in HER2-Positive breast cancer cells
pmc-12638914.creator: Sevda Jafari, Alireza Ostadrahimi, Afsaneh Farjami, Soheila Montazersaheb
pmc-12638914.description: HER2-positive breast cancer is an aggressive subtype with limited therapeutic options. Trastuzumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting the HER2 receptor, has improved clinical outcomes; however, its efficacy remains a critical challenge in the HER2-positive model. This study investigated the potential of chrysin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, to enhance the efficacy of trastuzumab in HER2-positive SKBR3 and BT-474 breast cancer cells.

pmc-13101640.title: Systemic immune-inflammatory index predicts all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in metabolic syndrome: A prospective cohort study using NHANES data
pmc-13101640.creator: Yao Sun, Shuguang Yang, Zengli Xiao, Youzhong An, Huiying Zhao
pmc-13101640.description: Highlights•SII is a cost-effective indicator for Metabolic Syndrome (MetS).•MetS patients exhibit significantly higher SII scores than healthy peers.•High SII predicts increased all-cause and CVD mortality in MetS.•A J-shaped relationship exists between SII and MetS mortality risks.•SII mortality prediction is strongest in MetS patients aged ≥60.

pmc-13140993.title: Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis of Vixarelimab in Healthy Volunteers and Patients With Chronic Pruritic Conditions
pmc-13140993.creator: Fei Tang, Steve Dang, Audrey Arjomandi, Lin Pan, Joy Hsu, Smita Kshirsagar, Nastya Kassir
pmc-13140993.description: Vixarelimab is a first‐in‐class fully human monoclonal antibody targeting oncostatin M (OSM) receptor beta (OSMRβ). It has been evaluated in Phase 1 and 2 studies in healthy volunteers and patients with chronic pruritic conditions and demonstrated anti‐pruritic efficacy in a Phase 2 study in prurigo nodularis, but detailed pharmacokinetic analysis has not been previously reported.

pmc-13556521.title: 410. Comparative neurophysiological signatures of psychedelics, stimulants and anesthetics in rodent cortical activity
pmc-13556521.creator: B Richardson, J O'Byrne, V Bruno, S Comai, R Carhart-Harris, G Gobbi
pmc-13556521.description: BackgroundPsychedelics induce altered states of consciousness (AOC) with profound perceptual, cognitive, and emotional shifts, often linked to positive therapeutic outcomes. Although serotonergic psychedelics such as psilocybin, LSD, and 5-MeO-DMT share receptor targets, they differ in behavioral and neural effects. How these compounds alter cortical dynamics relative to other consciousness-modulating agents, including dopaminergic stimulants and anesthetics, remains unclear.

pmc-13585727.title: TCF4 at the crest of development: a zebrafish model to explore craniofacial and gastrointestinal defects in Pitt-Hopkins syndrome
pmc-13585727.creator: Martina Orefice, Francesca Remondino, Irene Pieraccioni, Giulia Salamone, Silvia Savoli, Antonio Vitobello, Chiara Gabellini, Michela Ori
pmc-13585727.description: BackgroundPitt-Hopkins Syndrome (PTHS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of the TCF4 gene. It is characterized by intellectual disability, distinctive facial features, breathing abnormalities, and gastrointestinal dysfunction. While the role of TCF4 in central nervous system development has been extensively investigated, the developmental basis underlying craniofacial and enteric alterations remains poorly understood.
